title: Normalized inverse image of represented diagrams on subcanonical sites
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to the sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Assume each has finite limits and is subcanonical, meaning every presheaf $h_V=\operatorname{Hom}(-,V)$ is a sheaf of sets. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve finite limits and coverings, and let $L\dashv u^s$ be its geometric inverse-image adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], where $(u^sF)(V)=F(uV)$. For $V\in\mathcal C$ define $\beta_V:h_V\to u^sh_{uV}$ by $\beta_V(W)(a)=u(a)$, and let $c_V:Lh_V\to h_{uV}$ be its adjunct. Then $c_V$ is an isomorphism, natural in every arrow $a:V\to V'$:
$$c_{V'}\circ L(h_a)=h_{u(a)}\circ c_V.$$
For every finite diagram $V_j$ of objects of $\mathcal C$, these comparisons identify its image under $Lh$ with the diagram $h_{uV_j}$ and identify its finite-limit cones under the canonical finite-limit comparisons. In particular, if an object $G$ has multiplication $G\times G\to G$, unit $1\to G$ and inverse $G\to G$ satisfying the group identities, $c_G$ is an isomorphism of the resulting group sheaves, compatible with all homomorphisms between such represented group objects. The adjunct of $c_V$, evaluated at $\mathrm{id}_V$, is $\mathrm{id}_{uV}$.

proof.text: Use the already proved Adjunction.uliftYonedaCompIso from WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteLocallyConstantEtale.PullbackYoneda. It is the inverse of uliftYonedaCompHom, whose composition with any g evaluates under K.uliftYonedaEquiv to the Yoneda evaluation of adj.homEquiv(g). In particular, composing uliftYonedaCompHom with the comparison c gives the identity. Applying this identity and injectivity of J.uliftYonedaEquiv proves adj.homEquiv(c_V)=beta_V: both evaluations at id_V equal id_(U V), using U.map_id.

proof.text: Apply limit.hom_ext to the two canonical finite-limit comparison composites. At every projection, limMap_pi and preservesLimitIso_hom_pi reduce the equation to naturality of c on limit.pi V i, which is step 3. This works for every finite shape, including the empty shape, because limit.hom_ext covers it as well. Yoneda preserves limits by Mathlib.Sites.PreservesLimits and U and L preserve finite limits by the stated typeclass hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Functor.mapGrpNatIso to the existing natural isomorphism c. In cartesian monoidal categories every natural transformation of monoidal functors is monoidal, so no additional compatibility assumption is needed. The underlying hom and inverse components of the lifted isomorphism are definitionally c.hom and c.inv, respectively; both specified equations are reflexive.

This uses the adjunction from lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor (hypotheses match: C has finite limits, u preserves finite limits and coverings), the presheaf-naturality clause of the Mathlib leaf lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection, and full subcategory from def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology. Step 4: the represented-cone limit argument is written out; u and L both preserve finite limits; uniqueness of maps into a limit identifies c_T with the canonical comparison; the empty diagram is covered. Step 5: the group operations, the inverse of c_G and represented homomorphisms all follow, with no commutativity used. Small cases checked: u=id, terminal site, empty diagram, trivial and non-abelian G, non-full u.
